subject: Re: Short-term quota lift request for upcoming launch
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@byteframe.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@byteframe.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Short-term quota lift for upcoming launch

Hi Vivek,

Hope you’re well — we’re going live with a targeted marketing push on July 27 and our telemetry indicates a potential 8-10x spike in inference traffic for a 72-hour window. This is a hard launch for a paid feature so we need predictable throughput.

Can Redwood provide a short-term quota/rate increase or burst capacity for July 26–29? If so, what are the pricing paths (temporary rate increase vs. overrun true-up vs. prepaid burst credit)? Also need confirmation on whether there will be any change to tail latency or SLOs during the burst.

I’ve attached our projected traffic report and historical usage. Happy to set up a quick call today if needed.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform
ByteFrame Labs
attachment: traffic_report_q3.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@byteframe.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:03:01 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term quota lift for upcoming launch

Hi Elaine — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. We can support the window you describe; two practical options depending on how ByteFrame wants to handle billing/risk:

1) Temporary rate-limit increase (recommended for short windows): we can raise your per-route token-rate ceiling for a defined 72-hour window (Jul 26 00:00 UTC — Jul 29 00:00 UTC). Pricing: prorated usage at standard per-token rate + an operational uplift fee of 12% to cover prioritized routing and capacity reservation. No latency change expected; traffic will be routed to reserved burst capacity.

2) One-time burst credit + overrun true-up: we can issue a one-time burst credit (prepaid) that covers X tokens. Any usage beyond the credit is invoiced as an overrun true-up at your standard rate, but we can offer a 10% volume discount on the overrun if you (a) commit to a 3-month minimum post-launch usage band or (b) agree to a follow-on quarterly commitment by Aug 15.

Operational notes: we’ll enable prefix caching and aggressive batching for the route during the window to preserve latency SLOs. Monica (cc’d) will run a brief config check against your route to ensure rollout safety.

Next steps: tell me which option you prefer and confirm the exact UTC window you want us to enable. If you want the discounted true-up path, we’ll need an approved commercial note from finance (Aditya) and a one-page addendum.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachment: (none)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:18:47 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term quota lift for upcoming launch

Looping in finance: happy to support a discounted true-up if ByteFrame signs a 3-month commit at 60% of their projected post-launch usage. Proposed commercial concession: 15% discount on overrun true-up (instead of 10%) if the commit is signed within 7 days and the customer prepays 50% of the committed minimum. Otherwise stick with Vivek’s standard 10% discount for a Q commitment.

From an approvals perspective: I’ll need a short commercial note and an ARR estimate; if we go the burst-credit route we can treat the credit as an advance against the first invoice.

-Aditya
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@byteframe.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@byteframe.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:45:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term quota lift for upcoming launch

Thanks Vivek — we’d like to take Option 1 (temporary rate-limit increase) for the initial launch window to keep billing simple. Please enable Jul 26 00:00 UTC — Jul 29 00:00 UTC.

A couple of clarifying asks before we finalize:
- Can you confirm a written note that the uplift fee will be waived if the uplift fails to deliver 95% of the requested capacity?
- Will we see any billing changes on the invoice line items (we’re passing cost to product owners and need a clean line)?
- Can you confirm how the reserved capacity is billed vs. consumed tokens?

Attached are the load test results from our staging run for your reference.

Elaine Park
Head of Platform, ByteFrame Labs
attachment: load_test_results.csv

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@byteframe.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 11:03:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term quota lift for upcoming launch — confirmation and terms

Elaine — thanks for confirming. Below is a written summary we can attach to your invoice and to the HubSpot deal record. I’ve also attached a one-page term sheet (burst_terms_v1.pdf) and a DocuSign link for the short addendum if you want the discount path: https://docusign.com/tx/ABC12345

Summary (Jul 26 00:00 UTC — Jul 29 00:00 UTC)
- Action: Temporary per-route token-rate ceiling increase to accommodate projected 72-hour traffic spike.
- Billing: usage charged at standard per-token rate, prorated for the window, plus a 12% operational uplift applied to usage during the burst window. The uplift appears as a separate invoice line item labeled "Burst operational reservation fee".
- SLA/Capacity: Redwood will route your burst traffic to reserved capacity. If Redwood cannot deliver at least 95% of the requested capacity during the window, Redwood will credit the uplift fee for that window (refund/credit on the next invoice).
- True-up/overrun: If actual consumption exceeds projected numbers materially and you did not elect a prepaid burst credit, overrun is billed on the next invoice as "Overrun true-up" at the standard rate. Finance (Aditya) has pre-approved a 10% discount on overrun true-ups if ByteFrame signs a 3-month follow-on commit by Aug 15; a 15% discount is available if ByteFrame prepays 50% of the committed minimum within 7 days.
- Next steps: Monica will perform a config safety check today and we will enable the rate change on Jul 26 00:00 UTC. I’ll attach the term sheet and push a HubSpot note: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890

We’ll also include a clearly labeled invoice line so your product finance team can allocate costs. Let me know if you want the DocuSign addendum or prefer to proceed without a contract change (Option 1 only).

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
